title: Film-capacitor self-healing: clearing electrodes rescue thin high-k capacitors
idea: Industrial power film capacitors last 30 years because a thin metallization vaporizes around any breakdown spot and isolates it. Build MIM capacitor arrays with a 3-5 nm Al or Ti top-electrode skin that burns back locally under a forming pulse, healing weak spots before a TiN cap goes on, and measure yield versus dielectric thickness in a university fab.
why: Lets ZrO2 stacks thin ~20-30% (higher Cs or shorter pillars) without leakage-tail failures, meaning fewer Zr precursors and less high-AR etch per bit.

title: Self-oxidized TiN skin seeds rutile titania capacitor dielectric
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: oxidize the top 1-2 nm of the TiN bottom electrode with a controlled O3/plasma pulse into rutile TiO2 that serves as its own template, then grow Al-doped TiO2 by ALD so it crystallizes as rutile (k ~80). The whole stack is Ti, Al, N and O.
why: Breaks the 'smaller cell but more charge' contradiction without Ru templates or Hf/Zr. k ~2x ZAZ gives ~2x Cs, or the pillar aspect ratio can fall from ~70:1 to ~40:1.

title: Substitute manganese-aluminum and oxidized copper for platinum-group MRAM layers
idea: Build spin-orbit-torque memory from a perpendicular tau-MnAl free layer, an oxidized-copper (CuOx) spin-current source and a Mg-Al-O tunnel barrier, eliminating Pt, Ir, Ru, Ta and W from the stack.
why: Gives DRAM-class, refresh-free nonvolatile working memory from abundant elements only, removing the platinum-group metal inventory that limits MRAM scale-up.

title: Spalled 20-micron device films reuse each Czochralski donor fifteen times
idea: First principles: a DRAM die's devices live in the top <1 um of a 775 um wafer, so >99.8% of the high-purity silicon (and the quartz-crucible life that grew it) is mechanical ballast. Grow a 20 um epi layer, peel it off with a Ni-stressor controlled spall, bond it to a low-grade recycled handle wafer, then CMP and re-epi the donor for ~15 reuse cycles.
why: Cuts high-purity-quartz crucible and polysilicon intensity per wafer start ~10x (Spruce Pine chokepoint) and CZ energy per bit ~10x; the added bond/CMP cost per wafer is the trade.

title: Neuron-membrane ionic double-layer storage capacitor
idea: A neuron stores charge across a 4 nm membrane using ions, not a thick high-k oxide. Replace the 60-75:1 pillar with a planar cell that stores charge in the electric double layer at a TiN/solid proton-conductor interface (phosphosilicate glass or a CsH2PO4-type solid acid), reaching 10-30 uF/cm2 versus ~3 uF/cm2 for ZAZ, sealed by an ion-blocking ALD cap so ions never leave the cell.
why: Removes the HAR capacitor etch (fluorocarbon gas, etch tools, energy) and the Hf/Zr dielectric; 5-10x areal capacitance could flatten the cell. The open risks are ion relaxation speed (<10 ns needed) and leakage.

title: Venus-lander silicon carbide gain cell: retention measured in years
idea: NASA's SiC JFET ICs have run for a year at 460 C in Venus conditions, and at room temperature the same 3.3 eV bandgap makes storage-node leakage ~1e-21 A. Build a 2T SiC gain cell that stores charge on a JFET gate junction, so memory needs no refresh, no capacitor dielectric and no tungsten.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and hafnia/zirconia capacitors; serves 200 C industrial, automotive and space tiers now, and gets cheaper as EV demand drives SiC wafer costs down.

title: Redox polymer brushes store capacitor charge in shallow holes
idea: Scale jump from dielectric capacitor to molecule: a ~10 nm brush of poly(vinylferrocene) or porphyrin redox polymer grafted on a TiN electrode stores charge faradaically, roughly 100 uC/cm2 at 1 V, which is ~15x a ZAZ capacitor. A shallow 10:1 hole would then hold ~5 fF, with a solid polymer electrolyte cap.
why: Eliminates HAR etch and Hf/Zr dielectrics using Fe, C and H. Redox kinetics (ns vs us) and solid-state retention are unproven.

title: Iron spin-crossover molecules as electrically switched bistable bits
idea: Inverts 'memory materials must be inorganic crystals made in vacuum tools': use iron(II) spin-crossover complexes (Fe, N, C, H) with room-temperature hysteresis, switched between high- and low-spin states by field-induced ligand distortion and read by their volume and conductance change in a crossbar.
why: Bistable without power, so zero refresh; synthesized in solution from abundant elements and printed, with no W, Hf or PFAS.

title: Pillar-first, dielectric-last molybdenum wiring
idea: Reverse the damascene order: blanket-deposit molybdenum, subtractively etch pillars and lines, then gap-fill oxide around them instead of filling metal into dielectric holes with WF6 CVD.
why: Replaces tungsten contacts/plugs with Mo, which the U.S. mines domestically (Colorado), and removes fill seams and fluorine attack; ~100% W displacement in contacts with equal or lower resistivity at sub-20 nm.

title: Po holes arrange themselves: anodic-alumina template with anodized-titanium dielectric
idea: Po: 'holes that arrange themselves.' Extracted: anodize a sputtered aluminum film so it self-organizes into a hexagonal array of 30-60 nm pores microns deep, sputter or CVD titanium into the pores and anodize it into a conformal TiO2 dielectric; the self-ordered pores give each 180 nm cell many sub-litho capacitor tubes.
why: Charge wall and litho-bound scaling: ~10-20x capacitor area per cell footprint without EUV, ALD or hafnium; aluminum and titanium are abundant and U.S.-produced.

title: Tool-level helium recapture loops with polymer membranes
idea: Box [helium lever: recapture | location: each etch chamber exhaust | purifier: PIM-1/polyimide membrane + small compressor | return: chuck supply line]: collect He from electrostatic-chuck backside leaks and leak-test exhaust, purify it to 5N at the tool and recycle it, buying cylinders only for makeup.
why: Helium (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026): recovers ~80-90% of fab helium use and insulates DRAM output from the shortage; payback likely <2 years at current prices.

title: Abatement waste heat drives membrane distillation back to ultrapure water
idea: Combine the fab's 50-80 C waste heat (thermal abatement, compressors, heat-pumped chiller return) with membrane distillation: rinse and scrubber effluent passes against a PFAS-free polypropylene/ceramic hydrophobic membrane so only vapor crosses, yielding near-UPW feed that needs only final ion-exchange polishing.
why: Recovers 60-80% of rinse water with free heat, cutting fresh intake 2-3x and RO pumping energy; makes arid U.S. sites viable.

title: Hydrogen backside wafer cooling replaces helium in etch chucks
idea: Worsen: make every etch and deposition chuck bleed Qatari helium as backside coolant and use helium mass-spec for every leak check. Flip: run backside cooling on low-pressure (~10 Torr) pure H2, whose thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/mK) beats He (~0.15), in a sealed, interlocked chuck loop with a Pd-membrane purifier, and switch leak checks to H2/N2 forming-gas sensors.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% of supply offline): removes the largest helium use in a DRAM fab, cutting fab He demand ~70-90% with no change to thermal control.

title: Helium-as-a-service loop with per-tool recovery skids
idea: Worsen: vent every liter of helium after one pass through a chuck or leak test. Flip: fit each tool with a membrane plus PSA recovery skid and have a third-party operator own the helium inventory, billing fabs per liter lost, so >90% recovery becomes the operator's profit motive.
why: Helium chokepoint: fab purchases fall ~90%, and incentives line up with recovery rather than sales.

title: LCD panel fabs build capacitor-free memory on Gen-8 glass
idea: Display fabs pattern oxide TFTs on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass at a tiny fraction of wafer cost per area. Adapt idle Gen-6/8 oxide lines to make capacitor-free gain-cell memory sheets that are diced into tiles and bonded as a capacity tier behind CXL controllers.
why: No Czochralski crystal, quartz crucible, EUV or helium-intensive deep etch. It suits bulk far-memory capacity where density per area matters less than cost per area; density at ~0.5-1 um rules is the main limit.

title: Child asks why photoresist needs Teflon chemistry: carborane acid generators
idea: Persona: a child asks why the 'ink' needs the same stuff as non-stick pans. Replace perfluoroalkyl-sulfonate photo-acid generators with sulfonium salts of closo-carborane anions (CB11H12-). These superweak, non-coordinating boron-carbon anions give strong photo-acids with zero fluorine.
why: PAGs are a hard PFAS use in DUV and EUV resists that faces EU bans. Carborane anions keep the acid strength and low diffusion that 12 nm patterning needs.

title: Cultured quartz from oscillator industry crushed into crucible sand
idea: The quartz-oscillator industry grows ultra-pure cultured quartz in hydrothermal autoclaves, using low-grade quartz as nutrient. Run large autoclaves purely for crucible feedstock, then crush and acid-leach the cultured bars into <10 ppm-impurity HPQ sand.
why: Turns abundant low-grade quartz into Spruce Pine-equivalent purity, ending dependence on a single deposit. The risk is autoclave throughput and cost.

title: Reusable foundry molds: nitride crucibles pull many ingots each
idea: Metal foundries replaced one-shot sand molds with permanent molds for volume castings. Make dense reaction-bonded or CVD-coated silicon nitride crucibles that molten silicon does not wet and that survive cooldown, so one crucible serves 10+ pulls; the slight nitrogen pickup doubles as the intentional N-doping DRAM wafer makers already use to engineer vacancy defects.
why: Quartz crucibles devitrify and crack on cooldown and are single-use; a 10x reusable crucible cuts HPQ demand per ingot ~90% and turns a scarce consumable into durable capital.

title: UV-LED retrofit kits strip rare-gas lamps from legacy steppers
idea: Box [product: drop-in 365/385 nm LED illuminator | target: installed i-line steppers | layers: non-critical DRAM masks (implant blocks, pads, periphery) | model: per-layer service fee]: replace Hg arc lamps, whose bulbs carry Xe/Ar fill, with long-life LED arrays that switch instantly.
why: Removes rare-gas consumables and mercury from the ~30-40% of DRAM mask layers that are non-critical and cuts their litho energy ~60%; also sells to 200 mm fabs.

title: Substitute molybdenum for tungsten in buried wordlines and contacts
idea: Deposit buried wordlines and storage/bitline contacts by ALD/CVD molybdenum from MoO2Cl2 instead of tungsten from WF6; Mo needs no thick TiN barrier or nucleation layer, so more of the narrow trench is conductor. Source Mo from US primary mines (Climax, Henderson) and copper-mine byproduct.
why: Removes the China ~80% tungsten chokepoint; ~20-30% lower wordline resistance at <10 nm widths allows shallower recess gates with less GIDL leakage (refresh tail). Resource step change, modest energy gain.

title: Colorado molybdenum replaces Chinese tungsten in wordlines and contacts
idea: Minify tungsten to zero: convert buried wordlines, bitline contacts and landing pads to Mo from domestic Climax/Henderson ore, with a US-built MoO2Cl2 precursor plant. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower line resistance than W below ~15 nm.
why: Removes the ~80% China tungsten dependence and lowers wordline RC; a combined supply-chain and materials strategy.

title: Moly roaster to wordline: Colorado molybdenite becomes a tungsten-free metal
idea: Integrate like a steel mill from ore to coil: roast Climax/Henderson molybdenite concentrate to MoO3, chlorinate it on site to MoO2Cl2 CVD precursor, and deposit fluorine-free molybdenum fill for buried wordlines, bit-line contacts and periphery plugs.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%, no U.S. mine operating) from the whole flow; Mo has lower resistivity than W in narrow lines and the U.S. is a top-three Mo producer.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from Colorado ore
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero tungsten (China ~80%). Fill the buried wordline trench by MoO2Cl2/H2 CVD of molybdenum directly on the work-function liner, dropping the TiN barrier because Mo needs no protection from fluorine, and source the precursor from U.S. Climax/Henderson molybdenum.
why: Removes WF6 and fluorine gate damage; Mo's short electron mean free path gives ~20-40% lower line resistance below 15 nm and reclaims ~2 nm of trench for metal; the supply is domestic.

title: Deep-eutectic solvent cascade recovers metals from designed-open packages
idea: Worsen: incinerate memory boards and lose Ru, Hf, Ta, Au and Pd to slag. Flip: design packages with solvent-accessible layers, then dissolve them in a sequence of choline-chloride deep-eutectic solvents that selectively leach Au/Pd, then Cu, leaving Ru/Ta/Hf residues for electrowinning.
why: Precious and critical metal recovery at low temperature with little water: turns scrap DRAM into a domestic mine.

title: All-zinc ferroelectric FETs on glass: wurtzite ZnMgO gate on ZnO
idea: 1T FeFETs die on the ferroelectric/semiconductor interface: traps, depolarization and a parasitic interlayer that eat retention and endurance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O has been reported ferroelectric and is lattice-matched to ZnO, so sputter a coherent ZnMgO gate on a ZnO channel on glass with no interfacial oxide, and run it as a nondestructive-read cell needing only seconds-to-days retention.
why: Zinc and magnesium are abundant and widely sourced (no Hf, In, Ga, Pb); 1T cell with nondestructive read removes the capacitor and the restore cost of destructive read; DRAM-class duty needs far less retention than flash-class FeFETs failed to deliver.

title: Panel DRAM: memory arrays built on Gen-6 display glass
idea: Inverts 'memory is built on round single-crystal wafers': use idle LCD/OLED panel lines (1.5x1.8 m glass) with seed-directed excimer-laser-crystallized large-grain silicon access devices and stacked MIM capacitors to build a slower bulk-capacity tier, with small CMOS periphery dies bonded at the panel edge.
why: Glass needs no Cz crystal or quartz crucible; one panel is ~30x a 300 mm wafer and display capacity is underused; target 3-5x lower capital per bit for a capacity tier.

title: Silicon-free DRAM on glass panels in idled display fabs
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero silicon wafers. Make 1T1C memory with oxide-TFT access transistors and stacked MIM capacitors on Gen-8.5 glass panels in under-used display fabs, stacking 4-8 cell layers to offset the ~1 um design rule, and pair it with a small CMOS controller.
why: A 5.5 m2 panel has ~75x a 300 mm wafer's area and uses float glass instead of CZ silicon, HPQ crucibles or EUV; it targets a low-cost CXL far-memory tier rather than HBM.

title: Downhole-tool silicide: fully silicided titanium buried wordlines without tungsten
idea: 200 C downhole electronics favor refractory silicides that stay stable when hot. Fill the recessed gate trench with doped poly-Si and convert it fully to C54 TiSi2 (or NiSi) by RTA, with the TiN barrier doubling as work-function metal, all with university-fab sputter and RTA tools.
why: Removes W and WF6 from buried wordlines using abundant Ti and Si; fully silicided lines reach ~15-20 uOhm-cm, competitive with W in narrow trenches.

title: Arctic pipeline engineer cools etch chucks without PFAS fluids
idea: Persona: an Arctic engineer who keeps pipelines flowing with CO2 and hydrocarbons. Replace Novec/Fluorinert chiller fluids, discontinued in 3M's PFAS exit, with direct-expansion CO2 (R744) evaporators in the chuck for -60 C to +20 C. Use synthetic isoparaffin loops for warmer stages.
why: Removes PFAS heat-transfer fluids, which carry high GWP and ban risk, from the cryo-etch fleet that cuts DRAM capacitor holes.

title: Glass-core interposers replace ABF build-up in memory packages
idea: Minify the organic substrate: use borosilicate glass cores with laser-drilled through-glass vias as the package and interposer for memory stacks, CTE-matched to silicon (~3 ppm/K).
why: Removes the single-supplier ABF film. Glass's near-zero warp passes 125 C/10-year thermal cycling better than organic laminate, and it is made from sand.

title: Chewing gum: tree-latex and sugar resists with non-fluorinated acid generators
idea: Stimulus 'chewing gum' (chicle tree latex plus sugar) -> build a chemically amplified resist on bio-derived terpene/sugar polymers (cyclized polyisoprene or trehalose-ester backbones) with a non-fluorinated sulfonium camphorsulfonate photoacid generator and aqueous development.
why: Removes PFAS from photoacid generators and topcoats, the main PFAS exposure in lithography, ahead of EU/US restrictions, using renewable feedstock.

title: Waterless-planet alien cleans DRAM wafers with no liquid at all
idea: Persona: an alien from a dry world. Replace RCA and SPM wet cleans with a dry sequence: anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor oxide strip, UV-ozone organics removal, and cryogenic argon/nitrogen aerosol jets for particles. Dry the high-AR capacitor arrays with supercritical CO2 so they do not collapse.
why: Cuts ultrapure water ~50-60% and wet chemicals. Supercritical drying also removes stiction collapse of 70:1 pillars, a yield gain.

title: Venusian alien builds silicon-carbide DRAM that remembers for years
idea: Persona: an alien from scorching Venus picks wide-bandgap silicon carbide. Build a 4H-SiC access transistor and buried capacitor. Intrinsic carrier density in SiC is ~1e-8 cm-3, so leakage falls many orders of magnitude below silicon's and charge persists for years unpowered. Uses U.S.-made SiC wafers.
why: Refresh-free, quasi-non-volatile DRAM that removes refresh energy (fact 3). Made from abundant Si and C. Risk: SiC/SiO2 interface traps.

title: Photo-electrochemical macropore capacitor wafer with thermal oxide-nitride dielectric
idea: Magnify a cheap old process: etch 100:1 macropores into n-type silicon by backside-illuminated HF anodization (no plasma, no EUV), line them with thermally grown ONO, and hybrid-bond this capacitor wafer to the transistor wafer.
why: ONO is among the most reliable dielectrics at 125 C, and capacitor wafers can come from depreciated U.S. 200 mm lines, with no hafnium, zirconium, PFAS or EUV in the capacitor.

title: Two-pass Czochralski purifies upgraded metallurgical silicon, then grows prime
idea: Combine purification and crystal growth (zero masks): a fast sacrificial pull from low-B/P upgraded metallurgical silicon dumps metals into the melt tail by segregation (k ~1e-5 to 1e-8 for Fe, Cu, Ni); the clean section is crushed and repulled as a slow prime ingot.
why: Skips most of the Siemens process (~50-100 kWh/kg, chlorosilane chemistry), roughly halving polysilicon energy; B/P must be removed upstream by slag refining.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods use capacitorless 4F2 cells stacked eight high
idea: At 77 K subthreshold swing falls to ~15 mV/decade and thermally activated leakage drops >1e10, so a bare ~0.05 fF transistor gate holds charge for hours and needs no capacitor, while Cu/Mo wire resistivity drops ~6x. Build 4F2 vertical gain cells in 8 decks and run memory sleds immersed in LN2 made from air (no helium).
why: No capacitor + 8 decks = ~10x density at similar wafer cost; refresh vanishes and ~0.4 V operation cuts CV2 ~6x, offsetting cooling power at system level.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods: cold kills leakage, so capacitors shrink
idea: Cryo-CMOS users at 77 K see junction and subthreshold leakage fall by 6+ orders of magnitude, so a few tenths of a fF holds charge for hours. Immerse memory sleds in LN2 made from air on site (not helium), with tiny planar or capacitorless floating-body cells, and recover cold through the data center's air-separation unit.
why: Removes high-k capacitor materials and high-AR etch, and makes refresh energy (fact 3) near zero; wire resistance also drops, partly offsetting the cooling penalty.

title: Prussian-blue ion-insertion cells electroplated at room temperature
idea: Effect: ion migration and intercalation. K+ moves between a near-zero-strain Fe-hexacyanoferrate open framework and a solid electrolyte, changing the Fe3+/Fe2+ ratio and the conductance of a three-terminal channel. The film is electrodeposited from water at 25 C, and its battery-grade fast ion kinetics allow sub-us switching.
why: Scarce-element and thermal-budget intensity: memory made from Fe, C, N and K; zero-strain lattice targets very high cycle life; no vacuum tools for the active layer.

title: Space-station water loop: 98% UPW recovery with vapor-compression distillation
idea: The ISS recycles ~98% of its water with vapor-compression distillation and catalytic oxidation. Build fab reclaim the same way: segregate rinse streams by contamination class, send low-TOC rinses straight back through UV/RO/EDI, and push high-TOC streams through mechanical-vapor-recompression distillation, targeting 90-98% reuse.
why: Water limits Arizona and Texas fabs: cuts withdrawal ~5-10x and opens water-scarce U.S. regions for siting.

title: Closed-loop recovery of tungsten, hafnium, zirconium from fab waste
idea: Ideal: scarce metals that never leave the fab. Closest: cold-trap and scrub unreacted WF6 and Zr/Hf amide precursors from ALD/CVD exhaust (ALD utilization is often <5%), chemically strip PVD shields and chamber kits, and ship recovered oxides to a domestic refiner for re-precursor synthesis.
why: Cuts net virgin W/Hf/Zr demand 50-80% and turns each fab into a domestic secondary mine against China W (~80%) and concentrated zircon supply.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD deposits 150 oxide tiers without vacuum or helium
idea: Vacuum pumps, load locks and chambers dominate deposition cost, not atoms (a 10 nm tier is ~0.2 mg per wafer). Move wafers under gas-bearing spatial-ALD heads at 1 atm in N2, depositing ZnO channel, Al2O3 dielectric and Al:ZnO electrode tiers in-line at ~$3 per tier per wafer.
why: 150 tiers add ~$450 (~10%) to a ~$5k wafer for ~10x bits; no helium, no vacuum pumps, only abundant elements.

title: Microbiologist breeds bacteria that mine tungsten from fab scrap
idea: Persona: a biologist who knows organisms concentrate trace metals. Engineer Shewanella or E. coli strains to display tungstate-specific binding proteins (TupA/ModA family) on their surface. Use them to adsorb WO4(2-) from leached spent sputter targets, CMP slurry, WF6 scrubber water and Idaho/Nevada scheelite tailings, then calcine the biomass to WO3 as feed for WF6 resynthesis.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%): makes a domestic recycling loop that stays selective at ppm levels, where solvent extraction is uneconomic.

title: Directionally solidified eutectic films freeze into aligned nanoscale wordline lamellae
idea: Ideal: wires that freeze into place. Closest: laser zone-melt a thin film of an abundant eutectic (Al-Al2Cu or NiAl-Mo) on an insulating substrate so directional solidification grows aligned conducting lamellae at 30-80 nm spacing set by scan speed (lambda^2 v = const); selectively etch one phase to leave parallel metal lines.
why: 100x: line patterning becomes a cents-per-m2 thermal process; combined with cheap tiered substrates it targets >=100x lower $/GB with abundant Al/Cu/Ni/Mo (no W). Trades lamellar faults (sparing) and period tolerance.

title: Cold-trap recovery of unreacted zirconium ALD precursors
idea: Within $1M/24 months: insert a temperature-staged cold trap between capacitor ALD chambers and their pumps to condense unreacted Zr/Hf amide precursors (often >90% of dosed mass), then fractionally distill and re-certify them; validate on one ZAZ tool.
why: Cuts Zr/Hf precursor purchases ~3-5x and abatement load, easing both precursor cost and nuclear-chain Hf/Zr supply.

title: Abundant-elements-only zero-refresh memory prize
idea: Inverts 'industry picks materials, then finds supply': a federal staged prize ($50M/$250M/$1B) for a memory cell with >=10-year retention, >=1e15 endurance, <=50 ns access and DRAM-level cost per bit, built only from a whitelist of US-sourceable elements (no He, W, Hf, Ga, In, PGMs or PFAS) and judged on wafer-level arrays.
why: Pulls many teams toward chokepoint-free, zero-refresh cells while paying only for results; seeds a domestic manufacturing base.

title: Coal miner's carbon memory: sp2 versus sp3 bond switching
idea: Persona: a coal miner who knows soot and diamond are both carbon. Store bits by field-driven conversion between insulating sp3 and conducting sp2 bonding in 5 nm tetrahedral amorphous-carbon films between carbon electrodes. A DRAM write-coalescing cache in front keeps each cell to 1e8 writes or fewer.
why: Non-volatile cell made of carbon only: no Ge, Sb or Te (PCM) and no Hf or Ta (ReRAM).

title: Retreaded memory: remanufacture DRAM dies from retired servers
idea: Like truck-tire retreading and auto-part remanufacturing, hyperscalers return 3-5 year old DIMMs to a line that desolders packages by IR reflow, retests at speed, re-bins by retention and speed, and rebuilds them onto new modules with spare dies and sparing-aware firmware for CXL memory-expansion tiers.
why: Every remanufactured GB saves all the wafer, helium, crucible, water and energy of new silicon; recovering 20-30% of retired server DRAM could add percent-level supply within a year with no fab.

title: Eliminate the package: wafer-scale DRAM shipped as unsawn memory wafers
idea: Design arrays with spare-tile routing so the whole 300 mm wafer acts as one memory device, then bond it face-to-face to a logic wafer or to a cold plate with edge connectors, skipping dicing, ABF substrates, solder balls, mold compound and per-die handler test.
why: Eliminates ABF build-up film (single supplier), Sn-Ag solder and gold; ~10-20% off cost per bit from back-end and massive native bandwidth.

title: Epitaxial nickel-disilicide buried bitlines for vertical-channel cells
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): cubic NiSi2 is lattice-matched to Si (0.4% mismatch), so form single-crystal NiSi2 at pillar bases by templated Ni diffusion, then overgrow Si to make 4F2 vertical-channel transistors over a metallic buried bitline.
why: Replaces W/TiN buried bitlines (no WF6) and enables 4F2 cells; Ni is abundant (U.S./Canada).

title: Capacitive deionization loops recycle dilute fab rinse water cheaply
idea: Effect: electric-double-layer electrosorption. Activated-carbon electrodes pull ions out of dilute rinse streams with energy that scales with the ions removed, unlike RO, which scales with water volume. Cascade CDI and EDI to return >90% of rinse water to the UPW plant, and recover energy on discharge.
why: Water and energy intensity of DRAM fabs: 2-3x lower purification energy for dilute streams and a large cut in fresh-water draw.

title: Po oxide is only grown, never etched: fluorine-free LOCOS flow
idea: Po: 'oxide may only be grown, never etched.' Extracted: define isolation and contact windows by local oxidation through nitride masks (LOCOS and poly-buffered LOCOS), etch silicon, poly and aluminum only with chlorine and bromine plasmas, strip nitride in hot phosphoric acid, and drop fluorocarbon oxide etches entirely.
why: PFAS and fluorinated greenhouse gases (CF4, C2F6, NF3; GWP 6,500-17,000) cut to near zero in a memory flow that 1990s tools support natively.

title: Liquid-CO2 dry cleaning: supercritical drying stops capacitor pillar collapse
idea: Dry cleaners replaced perchloroethylene with liquid CO2, and textile dyers now dye in supercritical CO2 with no water. After the capacitor-mold wet etch, swap the water/IPA rinse-dry for a supercritical-CO2 exchange-and-vent step so no liquid meniscus ever pulls 60-75:1 pillars together; a process-only change behind an unchanged DDR/HBM interface.
why: Capillary force causes pillar leaning and collapse; zero surface tension lets aspect ratio climb toward the ~115 needed (fact 1) for ~1.5x Cs and better yield, while cutting IPA and UPW per wafer.

title: Eliminate retention requirements: refresh-free banks for short-lived AI tensors
idea: The compiler tags tensors that live <1 ms (activations, pipeline gradients, short-request KV) into ephemeral banks built with ~1 fF low-aspect capacitors on 4x shorter bitlines at 0.6 V, never refreshed; the controller tracks age and copies out anything nearing its retention limit.
why: Removes the high-AR capacitor (PFAS etch, Zr) and refresh for those banks; ~5x lower bitline C times ~2.8x lower V2 gives >10x lower energy per access.

title: Sodium-beta-alumina double-layer capacitors give 4x charge per area
idea: An electric double layer is a ~0.4 nm capacitor: ~20 uF/cm2 (~200 fF/um2) versus ~60 fF/um2 for ZrO2 stacks. A 5 nm Na-beta-alumina solid electrolyte (ionic conductor, electronic insulator) gives RC = (t/sigma*A)*C of ~1 ns for a 0.2 fF cell, and non-Faradaic charging causes no chemical wear.
why: 4x capacitance density makes 3D lateral capacitors 4x shorter; with 32 tiers that is ~10x density using Na, Al and O. Room-temperature ion response is the risk.

title: Proton-electrolyte double-layer storage node multiplies capacitance per area
idea: Box [electric double layer in 3 nm phosphosilicate proton conductor | Si access | voltage SA | near-planar | CZ Si | ALD/sol-gel]: replace the high-AR dielectric capacitor with an electrode / proton-conducting glass / blocking-electrode stack where protons pile up within ~1 nm of the electrode, giving ~10-20 uF/cm2 versus ~4 uF/cm2 for ZrO2.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 3-5x areal capacitance could let an AR ~15 capacitor reach 5 fF with no hafnia/zirconia and no deep etch; ion response must beat 10 ns, which is the big unknown.

title: Po the capacitor is a battery: solid-electrolyte double-layer storage
idea: Po: 'the DRAM capacitor is a tiny battery.' Extracted: replace the high-k film with a few-nm solid proton conductor (e.g. hydrated phosphosilicate glass) between ion-blocking electrodes, storing charge in an electric double layer of ~10-20 uF/cm2; the ion conductor is engineered so the double layer forms in under 10 ns.
why: Capacitor charge wall: ~1.5-3x capacitance per area over ZrO2-based stacks without hafnium, letting the capacitor be much shorter; speed and leakage are the open questions.

title: Nanoporous-carbon ionic double-layer storage node
idea: Periodic-table walk, C (6): replace the dielectric capacitor with an electric double layer, a 5 nm-pore CVD carbon electrode filled with a nonvolatile ionic liquid or solid polymer electrolyte; ~10 uF/cm2 times internal pore area gives ~20-50 fF in a 30x30x300 nm volume, and ion transit across 5 nm pores is ~10-30 ns.
why: Breaks the k/AR charge wall using only C, H, N, O: 4-10x Cs at AR ~10, no Hf/Zr ALD.

title: Reusable mother wafer: grow, use, and peel thin epi films
idea: Ideal: a wafer that is never consumed. Closest: grow a 10-20 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon double layer of a premium Cz mother wafer, build the DRAM, bond it to a cheap reclaimed/metallurgical-grade carrier, cleave at the porous layer, re-polish and reuse the mother 10-20 times.
why: Cuts Cz crystal growth, HPQ crucibles, polysilicon and puller energy per wafer ~10x; de-risks concentrated wafer supply chains.

title: Eliminate low-order bits until needed: MSB-first bit-plane fetch
idea: Store tensors bit-plane transposed across sub-rows so the controller fetches the top 2-4 bit planes first; attention screening or early-exit logic requests the lower planes only for the ~5-10% of values that matter.
why: KV-cache attention moves ~8-12x fewer bits for the same answer, cutting energy per useful value and effective capacity demand.

title: Caterpillar-style remanufacturing harvests DRAM from retired servers
idea: Adapted from Caterpillar Reman's core-deposit model. Hyperscalers return DIMMs from 4-6-year-old servers for a credit; a reman line desolders DRAM packages, burns them in, screens them at derated timings and rebuilds them into modules for edge, PC and CXL-pooled capacity tiers.
why: Retired servers hold enormous DRAM volume. Recovering even 30% adds supply with zero new wafers, helium, quartz or tungsten, at perhaps 30-50% of new cost per bit.

title: Wire-bonded staircase stacks multiply trailing DRAM per package
idea: Borrow NAND's 16-high staircase stack at existing OSATs: thin trailing-node DRAM dies to 40 um, offset them in a staircase and wire-bond them to a shared substrate. That reaches 16-32 GB per package for capacity-tier modules without TSVs.
why: Avoids HBM's TSV tax (~3x wafer area per bit, 20-30% yield loss) for capacity uses, using existing assembly lines only.

title: Stonemason builds plasma chamber walls from local spinel, not yttria
idea: Persona: a medieval mason who builds with local stone. Replace yttria and YOF plasma-facing coatings with aerosol-deposited MgAl2O4 spinel or AlON. Both resist fluorine plasma and are made from U.S. magnesia and alumina.
why: Removes a rare-earth chokepoint (yttrium is >90% Chinese) from every etch chamber.

title: Landing pad and capacitor bottom electrode become one TiN body
idea: Combine the tungsten landing pad and the bottom electrode (zero added masks, same landing-pad mask): pattern the pads in TiN and grow the electrode cylinder conformally from them, so there is no W/TiN interface and no WF6 fill.
why: Removes one of the largest tungsten volumes per die and a resistive interface; fewer depositions; TiN's higher resistivity is harmless over the pad's short length.

title: Polysilicon-plant waste chlorides recast into synthetic silica crucibles
idea: Magnify a waste stream: hydrolyze the SiCl4 byproduct of Siemens polysilicon reactors into ultra-pure soot or sol-gel silica, then fuse it into crucible bodies and inner liners, so crucibles no longer need natural Spruce Pine quartz.
why: Breaks the >80% HPQ chokepoint with a US-domestic feedstock that is already purified and is currently a disposal cost; purity exceeds natural quartz.

title: Jet-engine MAX-phase ceramics as tungsten-free buried wordline conductor
idea: Aerospace uses MAX phases (Ti3SiC2, Ti2AlC), layered carbides that conduct like metals yet tolerate heat like ceramics. Deposit nanolaminate Ti2AlC/Ti3SiC2 by ALD supercycles plus a front-end crystallization anneal as buried-wordline and contact fill, exploiting their layered in-plane conduction to dodge the grain-boundary resistivity penalty that hurts tungsten below 10 nm width.
why: Replaces tungsten (China ~80%) with Ti, Al, Si and C, all abundant and domestic; targets W-parity wordline resistance at 8-10 nm widths.

title: Indium-free MgZnO wide-gap channel for gain-cell DRAM
idea: Worsen: build every next-generation oxide gain cell from indium and gallium that are refined mostly in China and subject to export controls. Flip: use amorphous Al-doped MgZnO deposited by spatial ALD as the channel. Its bandgap (~3.8-4.2 eV) is wider than IGZO's (~3.2 eV), which suppresses off-state leakage further.
why: In/Ga chokepoint and refresh energy: all-abundant elements with a U.S. supply. Longer retention could cut refresh ~10x if mobility of ~5-15 cm2/Vs is enough.

title: Confectioner's candy-like molecule: croconic acid ferroelectric memory
idea: Persona: a confectioner who knows sugar-acid crystals. Vacuum-sublime croconic acid (C5H2O5) into capacitor wells as the FeRAM dielectric and seal it with ALD Al2O3. This hydrogen-bonded organic ferroelectric switches by collective proton transfer (Ps ~20 uC/cm2) instead of ion displacement.
why: Non-volatile memory from C, H and O only. Deposition below 150 C allows many BEOL tiers. No Hf, Zr or Pb.

title: Sea-urchin self-sharpening CMP pad saves ceria slurry and diamond
idea: Sea-urchin teeth self-sharpen because layered fibres break away to expose fresh edges. Cast roll-to-roll CMP pads from aligned fibre-polymer laminates whose fibres erode at a set rate, renewing asperities without diamond conditioning and holding abrasive in fibre grooves so less slurry is needed.
why: Cuts ceria (rare earth, China-concentrated) and silica slurry use ~30-40%, removes diamond conditioner discs and extends pad life.

title: Taylor-wire woven memory: glass-coated amorphous microwires as bistable bits
idea: Revive the Taylor (1924) and Ulitovsky (1950s) process, which draws glass-coated amorphous Fe-Si-B microwires with near-perfect square hysteresis (a large Barkhausen jump), and weave them with copper word wires like a 1960s core plane. Each crossing segment flips only on coincident currents and gives a sharp sense pulse, and the bit pitch is set by wire diameter and weave rather than lithography.
why: No EUV and no masks at all; abundant Fe, Si, B and glass; textile-mill manufacturing in the US; infinite endurance, nonvolatile cold working tier; claims ~100x lower capex per bit than a fab, at lower density.

title: Rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes: k~90 without hafnium or ruthenium
idea: Inverts 'DRAM high-k must be ZrO2/HfO2 stacks on TiN or Ru': oxidize a molybdenum liner into a rutile MoO2 bottom electrode that templates low-temperature (<450 C) rutile TiO2 (k 80-110), with an Al-doped interfacial layer to suppress leakage.
why: Hits the k~70 requirement of the capacitor charge wall with Ti and US-mined Mo instead of Hf/Zr/Ru; ~2x capacitance at the same aspect ratio, or AR dropped from ~70:1 to ~40:1, cutting etch time and fluorocarbon gas use.

title: Po chips talk through their sides: edge-metallized DRAM die cube
idea: Po: 'dies speak through their edges, not their faces.' Extracted: lap 180 nm DRAM dies to ~100 um, laminate 32-64 of them with adhesive, polish one face of the stack, and sputter and photo-pattern sidewall bus lines that join edge-routed pads (the 1990s Irvine Sensors memory-cube approach).
why: HBM TSV tax and density: 32-64x bits per footprint with no TSVs, no hybrid bonding and no copper via fill, all on U.S. 200 mm-era tools.

title: Eliminate the wafer fab: oxide gain-cell memory on idle display-glass lines
idea: Build 2T0C oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 glass (~5.5 m2, ~75x a 300 mm wafer) in under-used LCD fabs with 1-1.5 um lithography, then dice tiles for a high-capacity, slower CXL memory tier.
why: Repurposes depreciated capacity with no crucible quartz, no EUV and a <400 C process; ~1/50 the processing cost per m2, offsetting much lower areal density.

title: Dopant-free Schottky tiers skip implant in buried 3D layers
idea: Implanters cannot reach buried tiers anyway, so remove dopants: use 6 nm undoped Si channels with nickel-silicide Schottky source/drain formed by lateral silicidation from the bitline hole, and set threshold by gate work function.
why: Thin dopant-free channels cut tier pitch to ~35 nm (150 tiers in 5 um, ~10x density) and remove arsine/phosphine and activation anneals. The Schottky leakage tail is the risk.

title: Southwest Airlines single-fleet logic for a minimal-tool capacitorless fab
idea: Southwest flies a single aircraft type to slash spares, training and maintenance. Adapt this by designing a capacitor-free cell flow (no pillar etch, no ZAZ ALD, no support lattice) that runs on ~6 standardized shallow etch, deposition and litho tool families, sharing spares, chamber kits and gases fab-wide.
why: Dropping the capacitor removes the most helium- and fluorocarbon-intensive tools. Fewer tool types cut capex ~25% and halve spares inventory and specialty-gas SKUs.

title: Chill first, etch second: ride on thermal inertia, no helium
idea: Reverse when cooling happens: pre-chill wafers cryogenically in the load lock and run short etch/deposition steps on the wafer's own thermal mass, replacing continuous helium backside gas with a time-budgeted temperature window.
why: Helium supply lost ~30% (Qatar offline since March 2026); removing backside-He for short steps could cut fab helium use ~50-70%.

title: Satellite-optics CO2-snow and supercritical CO2 cleaning replaces RCA rinses
idea: Spacecraft optics are cleaned with CO2 snow jets because liquids leave residues in vacuum. In a university fab, replace selected post-etch and pre-deposition SC1/SC2 cleans with CO2-snow particle removal and supercritical CO2 with co-solvent for residue strip, measuring particle adders and metals by TXRF.
why: Each RCA clean uses tens of liters of UPW plus acids; CO2 is a recycled industrial byproduct; target ~30% fewer wet steps and UPW use.

title: Hydrogen replaces helium as wafer backside coolant and carrier gas
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change, resolving 'need a high-conductivity heat-transfer gas' vs 'helium is scarce': switch electrostatic-chuck backside cooling and CVD/ALD carrier flows from He to H2 (D2 where isotope passivation helps) at 5-20 Torr, where H2 conducts heat as well as or better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Leak rates stay below the flammability limit by design, supply comes from on-site electrolysis, and exhaust goes to the existing burn abatement.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30%, offline since March 2026). Backside cooling and carrier gas are the largest fab He uses, so this could remove ~60-80% of fab He demand.

title: Purdue's 1990s silicon-carbide DRAM rebuilt on EV-glut SiC wafers
idea: Purdue built 4H-SiC DRAM cells in the 1990s with retention of hours or longer at room temperature, killed by expensive, micropipe-riddled SiC wafers. EV power electronics has since driven 200 mm SiC to low defect density and falling prices; build a planar or trench 1T1C cell on 4H-SiC whose 3.3 eV bandgap makes junction and GIDL leakage negligible.
why: Refresh essentially eliminated (16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth); SiC boules grow by sublimation in graphite crucibles, so no high-purity quartz; U.S. SiC capacity already exists; trades density (~28-40 nm rules) for energy and supply security.

title: Titanium-silicide strapped dual-work-function polysilicon wordline
idea: Combine the old poly gate with a self-aligned silicide strap (zero added masks): fill the buried-wordline trench with in-situ doped poly, recess it, then sputter Ti and anneal so TiSi2 forms only on exposed poly, leaving lower n+ poly near the channel and the strap for conduction.
why: Removes buried-wordline tungsten with abundant Ti and Si; work-function engineering of the poly reduces GIDL, lengthening refresh intervals.

title: Substitute laser cold-splitting for wire-saw wafering and lapping
idea: Focus a pulsed laser to write a subsurface damage plane inside the ingot, cleave a 300 mm wafer off with a polymer stressor or thermal shock, then use dry plasma stress relief instead of slurry lapping, wet etch and multi-step wet polish.
why: Wafer manufacturing spends hundreds of liters per wafer on saw coolant, lapping and cleaning; laser splitting cuts that >10x and saves ~40% kerf silicon, so each quartz crucible yields more wafers.

title: Recover ceria from spent CMP slurry
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench pilot that concentrates spent STI CMP slurry by ultrafiltration, dissolves silica fines in dilute caustic, recovers ceria by flocculation, and re-calcines it to abrasive spec for reuse.
why: Cuts purchases of China-concentrated rare-earth ceria by ~50-70% and reduces slurry waste, on existing CMP tools.

title: Drill bit: carbide-scrap microrefinery makes fluorine-free tungsten chloride precursor
idea: Stimulus 'drill bit' (worn cemented carbide) -> a 10-person microrefinery oxidizes and chlorinates scrap WC tool inserts and spent W targets into sublimation-purified WCl5/WCl6 for fluorine-free ALD/CVD tungsten.
why: Domestic recycled tungsten sidesteps China's ~80% share and removes WF6 handling; recycling already supplies ~30% of world tungsten.

title: One perfect donor, many cheap handles: layer-transfer DRAM wafers
idea: Reverse the substrate role: hydrogen-implant and cleave only the top 1-2 um of a prime CZ wafer onto low-grade polycrystalline or solar-grade handle wafers with a buried oxide barrier, then re-polish and reuse the donor 10-20 times.
why: Cuts prime-grade crystal (and therefore HPQ crucibles, polysilicon and furnace energy) per DRAM wafer by ~10x; the handle can come from abundant metallurgical-grade sources.

title: Grayscale nanoimprint cuts the 3D staircase in one etch
idea: A staircase carries one piece of information, a depth profile, yet costs N resist-trim/etch cycles; imprint a single tapered resist profile from a grayscale NIL master and transfer it with one 1:1-selectivity etch, exposing every tier's landing pad at once.
why: Removes ~N/2 litho-etch cycles for 150+ tiers, so tier count can grow ~10x without added staircase cost, while cutting resist (PFAS PAG) and etch gas per bit.

title: Dead-bank harvesting turns partial DRAM dies into lower-capacity SKUs
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: instead of scrapping dies whose repair redundancy runs out in a few banks, fuse those banks off. Sell the dies as 3/4- or 7/8-capacity parts with a mode register the controller maps around, as CPU makers do with harvested cores.
why: Raises usable bits per wafer ~2-6% at zero capital. The gain is largest for HBM, where one bad die scraps an entire stack.

title: Spinel and AlON plasma-facing coatings replace rare-earth yttria
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: coat etch-chamber walls, liners and focus parts with a graded stack: dense MgAl2O4 spinel or AlON at the plasma face, grading to Al2O3 at the substrate. Each layer is placed where its erosion resistance or adhesion is needed, replacing Y2O3 and YF coatings.
why: Removes yttrium (a China-dominated rare earth) from high-wear chamber parts and grades CTE to cut flaking particles. Uses only Mg, Al, O and N.

title: Substitute stealth laser dicing and dry polish in HBM stacking
idea: Thin HBM wafers by mist-cooled grinding plus fixed-abrasive dry polishing, and singulate them by internal stealth-laser modification plus tape expansion instead of water-flooded blade dicing.
why: Blade dicing and wet grinding run continuous litres-per-minute flows; the dry route cuts back-end water >10x and reduces chipping that contributes to HBM's 20-30% yield loss.

title: Corn farmer's biochar supercapacitor lets DRAM survive outages
idea: Persona: a farmer who turns corn stover into biochar. Mount KOH-activated stover-carbon supercapacitors (~2000 m2/g) on each DIMM or HBM module, storing ~100-300 J. That is enough to flush DRAM into an on-module NAND shadow when power fails and restore it on boot: non-volatility by architecture.
why: Persistent memory at DRAM speed and cost with no lithium, cobalt or tantalum capacitors. It also replaces rack lithium-ion backup units.

title: Molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters store two quantized bits per node
idea: A 1 nm Keggin cluster [PMo12O40]3- accepts electrons in discrete redox steps ~0.2-0.4 V apart, so multilevel states are fixed by chemistry rather than by threshold variation. Graft a cluster monolayer as the floating storage node of a vertical gain cell, write levels with gate pulses and refresh like DRAM.
why: 2 bits per node, no capacitor, 4F2 vertical, 3 decks = ~10x density; Mo and P are abundant. Solid-state redox endurance is unproven.

title: Uranium-enrichment fluorine plants: on-site F2 replaces NF3 and fluorocarbons
idea: Uranium enrichment has made elemental fluorine electrolytically at ton scale for 80 years. Put modular KF-2HF electrolyzers at each fab: F2 replaces NF3 (GWP ~17,000) for chamber cleans and serves as a carbon-free fluorine-radical source, fed by HF recovered from fab fluoride wastewater.
why: Cuts PFC/PFAS-class gas use and GHG emissions; recycling wastewater HF eases fluorspar dependence (China ~60%).

title: Cold-wall skull crucible pulls 300 mm silicon without quartz
idea: Minify the crucible to nothing: melt silicon in a water-cooled, segmented copper induction crucible so a frozen silicon skull holds the melt, and pull Czochralski crystals from it. Electromagnetic stirring and partial levitation keep the melt off the cold wall.
why: Removes Spruce Pine high-purity quartz (>80% share) from ingot growth entirely and lowers interstitial oxygen; attacks the scarcest crystal-growth consumable.

title: Ramtron FeRAM without lead or platinum: aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric capacitors
idea: PZT FeRAM died on lead, Pt/Ir electrodes, 600 C anneals and a failure to scale below ~130 nm. Replace PZT with wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N (ferroelectric near x~0.07-0.15), sputtered below 400 C onto TiN or Mo electrodes, as a 1T1C cell whose ~100+ uC/cm2 remanent polarization needs only a short ~3:1 cup instead of a 60-75:1 pillar, refreshed only on power-down.
why: Removes Pb, Pt, Ir and the hafnium of HZO; Al, B and N are effectively unlimited and U.S.-producible; nonvolatile so standby refresh vanishes; ~20x shallower capacitor etch. Endurance of nitride ferroelectrics is the open risk.

title: Williams tube reborn: microcolumn e-beams write charge on blank plates
idea: Revive the 1947 Williams-Kilburn tube: an i-line-patterned array of field-emission microcolumns at 2 um pitch, in a sealed MEMS vacuum, each steers a ~10 nm spot over a 200x200-bit patch of an UNPATTERNED SiO2/Si3N4 storage plate. The beams write charge and read it back by secondary-emission current, so bit density comes from the beam spot, not from lithography.
why: No EUV and almost no patterning of the storage medium (fact 4: capital); no capacitors, Hf or W; claims a 10 nm bit pitch, near DRAM-class density, using only i-line tools.

title: Aquaporin-studded roll-to-roll membranes for ultrapure water reclaim
idea: Aquaporin channels pass about a billion water molecules per second while rejecting ions. Embed aquaporins or synthetic pillar[5]arene water channels in roll-to-roll-cast polyamide reverse-osmosis films for the UPW reclaim loop, running at about half the pressure of standard RO.
why: Cuts UPW energy ~30-50% and pushes water reclaim toward 90%, easing water intensity and drought siting for US fabs.

title: Millipede revived: thermomechanical probes on recyclable Diels-Alder polymer
idea: Revive IBM's abandoned Millipede: arrays of heated silicon cantilever tips write nanometer pits into a thermally reversible Diels-Alder polymer film and read them through the tip's thermal resistance change. The tip arrays are i-line patterned at 50 um pitch while the bits are 10 nm.
why: Density below the lithography limit without EUV; the medium is cheap organic polymer with no metals; a dense nonvolatile capacity tier that offloads cold DRAM pages; claims 1 Tb/in2 at microsecond access.

title: Barium-armored crucibles from non-Spruce Pine quartz
idea: Within $1M/24 months: coat the inner wall of crucibles made from lower-grade Norwegian or U.S. quartz with a barium-hydroxide wash that nucleates a dense, uniform cristobalite skin at melt-in to act as an impurity diffusion barrier; validate on a 4-6 inch lab puller with lifetime and oxygen metrology.
why: If the skin blocks alkali and Al outdiffusion, crucibles no longer need Spruce Pine (>80%) HPQ; lab pullers make the test affordable within the budget.

title: Eccles-Jordan flip-flop rebuilt from nanoscale vacuum-channel triodes
idea: Revive the 1918 vacuum-tube flip-flop at nanometer scale: cross-couple two field-emission vacuum-channel triodes (silicon tips, 50 nm sealed gaps, no gate dielectric) into a static latch. The vacuum gap has no dielectric leakage and no junctions, so the cell holds state without refresh and runs at 250 C.
why: Removes Hf/Zr dielectrics, implants and the leakage tail (fact 3); running hot lets data centers drop chillers, saving energy and water; claims refresh energy near zero.

title: Anderson's 1952 crossbar ferroelectric memory revived in hafnium-free AlBN
idea: Revive J.R. Anderson's transistor-less barium-titanate crossbar store using wurtzite aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric films (all abundant elements). Anderson's V/3 half-select scheme is combined with pulse shaping that exploits AlBN's very square loop to suppress disturb, and rows are read by switching current and then rewritten.
why: No hafnium/zirconium and no transistor per cell, which cuts periphery and scarce inputs; a 4F2 crossbar stacks in BEOL; the honest risk is endurance (1e6-1e9), so it serves as a nonvolatile working tier behind DRAM caches; claims 2x density at the same node.

title: Cartographer: the border is the bit in barium titanate
idea: Persona: a cartographer who knows borders carry the traffic. Write and erase charged conductive domain walls in thin BaTiO3. The bit is whether a wall bridges two electrodes, read non-destructively by its conductance.
why: Non-volatile with non-destructive read (fact 8). Barium comes from Nevada barite, and no Li, Nb, Hf or Pb is needed.

title: Capacitor-on-foil revived: giant-k barium titanate fired on nickel foil
idea: Fired capacitor-on-foil laminates for PCBs stalled on coarse patterning and lamination yield. Make the foil the memory substrate: fire a 300-500 nm BaTiO3 film (k~1,000-2,000) on nickel foil at ~900 C in reducing gas, then build oxide TFTs above it below 350 C, so each cell's capacitor is a flat ~1 um2 pad holding >10 fF (~30 fF/um2).
why: Solves the capacitor charge wall with k instead of AR 115: planar capacitors, no high-AR etch, no Hf/Zr; nickel foil is cheap; fire-first then TFT sequencing decouples thermal budgets.

title: MLCC co-firing on a carrier, then transfer the capacitor layer
idea: MLCC makers fire barium titanate layers at ~1100 C on carriers; fire a sub-100 nm relaxor (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr)O3 dielectric between conductive-oxide electrodes on a sacrificial carrier wafer, pattern a shallow 5:1 relief, then hybrid-bond and layer-transfer it onto the cold access-transistor wafer.
why: Decouples perovskite crystallization (k 300-1000) from the CMOS thermal budget, so a shallow capacitor reaches ~5 fF without 70:1 holes or hafnium/zirconium ALD; barium and titanium are abundant.

title: Carbide-scrap tungsten turned into domestic WF6
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench pilot that takes U.S. cemented-carbide scrap (drill bits, inserts) through the zinc reclaim process, oxidizes and hydrogen-reduces it to tungsten powder, fluorinates it with on-site F2, and distills 6N WF6 for wordline CVD.
why: Breaks the China ~80% primary-tungsten dependence for fab precursors using an existing domestic scrap stream; DRAM needs only tonnes, so a small plant covers a U.S. fab.

title: Datacenter DIMM salvage reborn as tested CXL memory pools
idea: Combine server decommissioning with CXL memory expansion: desolder DRAM packages from retired DDR4/DDR5 modules, retest and speed-bin them, and mount them on CXL Type-3 cards whose controller hides mixed timing and maps weak rows out.
why: Every reused retired bit displaces a new wafer start; at 4x prices, recovering even 5% of supply needs zero fab capital, zero helium and zero quartz.

title: Steel-mill air separation units retrofitted to capture neon
idea: Ukraine's semiconductor neon came from crude-neon columns on Soviet steel-mill air separation units. Adapt this by bolting crude neon/helium columns onto US integrated-steel and chemical-plant ASUs and purifying the output into excimer laser gas for the DUV ArF/KrF layers that still pattern most of DRAM.
why: Neon historically came ~50% from Ukraine/Russia. Capture at ~20 existing US ASUs could cover domestic fab demand without new air-separation capex.

title: Grow capacitor walls up instead of etching holes down
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: area-selective ALD grows the capacitor support lattice upward from seeded lines, so the 60-75:1 storage structure forms without a fluorocarbon high-aspect-ratio etch.
why: HAR capacitor etch is the heaviest user of PFAS-class fluorocarbon gases and NF3 chamber cleans; additive growth could cut those per wafer by >50% and relax the charge-wall aspect ratio limit.
